title: Catch conflicts between parallel agents editing one repository, without flagging everything
problem: When several agents work one repository in parallel, two of them can take decisions that cannot both hold: one moves a call behind a flag, another deletes the flag. Nothing notices, because the files they touched do not overlap, and the merge is clean. ARC compiles a repository into a typed artifact of claims with evidence and offers a merge that flags conflicting decisions across agents. Whether that catches real conflicts is unmeasured, including by its author. The trap sits in the metric: flagging every pair of edits catches all of them.
subject: https://github.com/PJuniszewski/ARC

acceptance.how: Both arms in one run. Your repo runs `make bench` over a public corpus of parallel agent edit sets with labelled conflicts (name it, pin the commit). It runs a file overlap baseline and your detector over the same sets and prints one JSON line: {f1, precision, recall, baseline_f1, n, n_conflicts}. The score is f1, and that is what refuses the flag everything answer, because precision collapses under it. Nothing may execute the repositories under test: this is static analysis of edits, and a run that imports or runs the corpus is void.
acceptance.metric: f1 - harmonic mean of precision and recall on labelled cross agent conflicts
